label: Game B
nuance_found: Score is a chain multiplier (x2 to x4, labels like DOUBLE, VIVID, BLOOMSTORM, BRILLIANT) that decays if you stop killing, so you keep moving and chain. BLOOM is a crowd-clear you hold until a pack gathers, then pop for a burst (+300, +200 popups). Dash makes you untouchable, so dashing through a pack is the escape. Dying costs only a tenth of the score (it dropped 63,909 to 57,518) and sends you back to a lantern, so risk is cheap. Inkwells need clearing before their glowing nodes open, so aggro first and then break nodes.
audio: A looping music bed the whole time plus small square-wave blips on kills; I never heard distinct gun or hit effects reported, so shots and deaths felt quiet.
furthest_progress: Score 74,286 at 540 s, 2.6% restored; Olive Terraces first inkwell broken, nodes broken, nest 1 of 8 done, then Millbrook village inkwell area entered; second inkwell not finished. Died about 6 times.
control_trouble: Two-thumb aiming with a 0.5 s view is rough: I overshot turns, lost the gold marker, got wedged in trees, and looked at sky or ground often. Auto-fire only helps once ink is in the crosshair. The long walks between fights are partly my bad steering.
best_moment: Bloom pop into a x4 chain at 5,990 with the grey valley flooding to colour around me.
worst_moment: Long empty walks across grey snow between fights, then getting killed by something I never saw while the screen turned pink.
verdict: Looks like a real product. The ink-to-colour reveal is the best visual trick I have seen on a phone game this session, and the multiplier chain gave me a score to chase within 35 seconds. It does let me play like an expert, because I can dash through and bloom a crowd. But the stretches between fights are dead, enemies drag, and I could not see my hits land with sound. Cheap deaths remove the tension. I would play a few more runs this week, so a 6 and a half, not a 7.
